Q: Java CLI Task Tracker project A:

I am creating a program that essentially tracks the users tasks. The issue I had was taking the user input and using that input in a switch statement for a particular case, when a string has a space.

For example:

The user enters "list todo" - they expect that command to list the tasks that need done in the CLI. The commands are read through the main method parameters.

public static void main(String[] args)

String[] args takes the command list todo as an array of strings.

args[0] = list

args[1] = todo

My switch statement never makes it to this string because of the space, so if a user types "list dodo", it immediately exits at the "list" case, because the switch statement only checked for args[0] (the command variable). I wanted to know how to fix this particular bug.

Hope that helps!

Q: Determine if an arbitrary regex matches the whole string A:

JavaScript sadly doesn't have a built-in method to test if a regular expression matches a whole string.

Since 2020, browsers all implement the .flags property, so the messy string manipulation of the original post and older replies is no longer needed. The naïve solution would therefore be:

new RegExp("^" + regexp.source + "$", regexp.flags).test(str)

However, this won't work with all regular expressions:

  • Expressions with a disjunction | need to be wrapped in a non-capture group (?: ) first.
  • In expressions with the m flag, ^ and $ will also match after and before a line break. On recent browsers we could wrap them with (?-m: ) to temporarily disable the m flag, but on older browsers there's not much we can do.
  • On expressions with a g or y flag, the behavior of .test(str) depends on and can mutate the value of .lastIndex. Our new RegExp should not have those flags, but silently discarding them is probably a mistake; whoever wrote the original expression must have used them for a reason.

For these reasons, I would suggest manually comparing the length of a match with the length of the string, and documenting the explicit behavior of your function when it comes to lastIndex and global/sticky regular expressions.

/**
 * Returns true if executing a RegExp on a string matches the whole string.
 * If the RegExp has the global flag, all matches will be joined before comparison.
 * The `lastIndex` property of the RegExp will be ignored and left unchanged.
 */
function completeMatch(regex, str) {
    const match = str.match(new RegExp(regex));
    return Boolean(match) && (regex.global ? match.join("") : match[0]).length === str.length;
}

Q: Can't see pages on page listing after Wordpress update A:

The issue might be the server's memory limit, which fails while trying to retrieve your data from database.

HOW TO CHECK

The error should be listed in your server logs. If it's not there, it's not a memory issue.

If you have access via SSH and your application is running on Apache, run one of the following:

less /var/log/apache2/error.log

or to enable real-time updates:

tail -f /var/log/apache2/error.log

If you see a line containing something like:

PHP Fatal error:  Allowed memory size of 268435456 bytes exhausted

it means you hit the memory limit.

QUICK SOLUTION

Despite the server configuration, Wordpress sets its own limit.

Add this line to your wp-config.php:

define( 'WP_MAX_MEMORY_LIMIT' , '512M' );

It won't solve the real problem, but it will allow you to keep Wordpress running while you check where the issue comes from.

See Wordpress Docs or this article for more methods.

IMPORTANT:

For anyone reading this answer:

256M is already a lot of memory for rendering a dashboard page. 512M is a huge amount of memory. Check if your application really needs all this memory.

The real problem might be caused elsewhere by Wordpress configuration or data.

To troubleshoot:

  • First switch to one of the default Wordpress theme and check that the issue isn't caused by your theme.
  • Then try removing plugins.
  • Lastly check the same theme/plugin configuration on a clean database.

Q: Using Python API libraries with the same name from multiple tool versions A:

For the moment I have gone with the following:

Sys.path.append(apiPath)
From ClientAPI import ClientAPI

Do some stuff

if apiPath in sys.path()
    sys.path.remove(apiPath)
if ClientAPI in sys.modules()
    del Sys.modules[CilentAPI]

It seems to work fine & I can swap between different versions.
The ClientAPI itself is able to give a feedback on its version so I can also check which version is loaded.
